question: Suppose \(x\) and \(y\) are two positive numbers satisfying the equation \(x^y=y^x\). Which of the following are true?

options.A: For all \(x>1\), there always exist a \(y>x\) such that the above equation holds;
options.B: For all \(x>e\), there is always a \(y>x\) such that the above equation holds;
options.C: For all \(1<x<e\), there is always a \(y>x\) such that the above equation holds;
options.D: If \(x<1\), then \(y\) must be equal to \(x\).

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
